questions.prompt: What is the critical lifetime pitfall of returning `std::string_view` from a function that constructs a local `std::string`?

options.text: The local `std::string` is destroyed on return, leaving the `std::string_view` dangling

questions.prompt: Why should you NOT write `return std::move(local_obj);` when returning a local variable by value?

options.text: It inhibits Named Return Value Optimization (NRVO / copy elision), forcing a move instead of zero-cost in-place construction
It turns the return into a copy

questions.prompt: In a function template `template <typename T> void f(T&& arg)`, what is `T&&`?

options.text: A forwarding (universal) reference that binds to both lvalues and rvalues and preserves value category via `std::forward<T>(arg)`

code.source:
template <typename T>
void relay(T&& x) { sink(std::forward<T>(x)); }

options.text: The Static Initialization Order Fiasco across translation units

They allocate intermediate `std::vector`s at every step

questions.prompt: What does `std::jthread` (C++20) add over `std::thread`?

options.text: Automatic `.join()` in its destructor (RAII) and cooperative cancellation via `std::stop_token`

questions.prompt: Why does `std::scoped_lock lock(m1, m2);` (C++17) prevent deadlock when locking multiple mutexes?

options.text: It uses a deadlock-avoidance algorithm to acquire `m1` and `m2` simultaneously without fixed-order assumptions

questions.prompt: When should you inherit a class from `std::enable_shared_from_this<T>`?

options.text: When a member function needs to create a `std::shared_ptr<T>` to `*this` sharing the existing control block

questions.prompt: What is Small String Optimization (SSO) in `std::string`?

options.text: Storing short strings inline inside the `std::string` object itself without a heap allocation

questions.prompt: What is a data race in C++, and what does the standard say about it?

options.text: Two threads accessing the same non-atomic memory location concurrently where at least one writes—it is Undefined Behavior

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `std::atomic<T>` in C++. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Provides race-free atomic loads, stores, and read-modify-write operations
`std::atomic_ref<T>` (C++20) can apply atomic ops to non-atomic objects temporarily
`volatile` is equivalent to `std::atomic` for thread communication

questions.prompt: What does the One Definition Rule (ODR) violation in C++ typically cause?

options.text: Undefined behavior or linker multiple-definition errors when two TUs see differing definitions of an inline function, template, or class

questions.prompt: Why is `std::unique_ptr` + `Pimpl` (Pointer to Implementation) used in C++ library headers?

options.text: To hide private fields/headers behind an opaque pointer, preserving ABI stability and minimizing header rebuilds

questions.prompt: In the Pimpl idiom with `std::unique_ptr<Impl> pimpl;`, why must `~Outer();` be declared in the header and defined (`= default`) in the `.cpp`?

options.text: Because `std::unique_ptr<Impl>`'s default deleter requires `Impl` to be a complete type at the point the destructor is instantiated

questions.prompt: What does `std::launder` or `std::start_lifetime_as` (C++23) address in low-level C++?

options.text: Pointer provenance and object lifetime rules when reusing raw storage or placement `new`

questions.prompt: What does `std::expected<T, E>` (C++23) model compared to `std::optional<T>`?

options.text: Either a successful value `T` OR a typed error value `E`, without throwing exceptions

questions.prompt: What is a subtle bug with `std::vector<bool>`?

options.text: It is a bit-packed specialization whose `operator[]` returns a proxy object rather than a real `bool&`, breaking generic code

questions.prompt: Why can `std::list` or `std::map` hurt CPU throughput compared to `std::vector` or flat hash maps for small/medium data?

options.text: Per-node heap allocations scatter nodes in RAM, causing frequent CPU cache misses during traversal

questions.prompt: What does `std::pmr::monotonic_buffer_resource` (C++17 `<memory_resource>`) provide?

options.text: A fast arena/bump allocator usable directly by `std::pmr::vector` and `std::pmr::string`

questions.prompt: What does `[[likely]]` / `[[unlikely]]` (C++20) communicate to the compiler?

options.text: Branch prediction hints to optimize hot-path instruction layout

questions.prompt: Select all true statements about `std::shared_ptr` thread safety. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Copying a `shared_ptr` locks the pointed-to `T` object
Incrementing/decrementing the control block's reference count from multiple threads is thread-safe
Concurrent reads/writes to the SAME `std::shared_ptr` instance without synchronization are a data race (use `std::atomic<std::shared_ptr<T>>` in C++20)
The pointed-to `T` object itself is NOT automatically thread-safe for concurrent mutation

questions.prompt: What is heterogeneous lookup in `std::map` / `std::unordered_map` (using `std::less<>` or transparent hash)?

options.text: Looking up a `std::string` key using a `std::string_view` or `const char *` without allocating a temporary `std::string`

questions.prompt: What does `std::bit_cast<uint32_t>(my_float)` (C++20 `<bit>`) replace safely?

options.text: Undefined-behavior pointer type-punning `*(uint32_t*)&my_float`, performing a `constexpr`-capable bit reinterpretation

questions.prompt: Why should destructors in C++ almost never throw exceptions (`noexcept` by default since C++11)?

options.text: If a destructor throws while another exception is already unwinding the stack, `std::terminate()` immediately aborts the process

questions.prompt: What does `std::exchange(ptr, nullptr)` return and do?

options.text: Replaces `ptr` with `nullptr` and returns `ptr`'s previous value—ideal for writing clean move operations

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of `std::source_location::current()` (C++20)?

options.text: Capturing file, line, and function name cleanly as default arguments without `__FILE__`/`__LINE__` macros

questions.prompt: What happens when `std::condition_variable::wait(lk, pred)` is called?

options.text: Atomically unlocks `lk`, sleeps until notified, re-locks `lk`, and loops until `pred()` returns `true` (handling spurious wakeups)

questions.prompt: What is false sharing in multi-threaded C++?

options.text: Two threads modifying independent variables that happen to sit on the same 64-byte CPU cache line, causing cache-coherency ping-pong

questions.prompt: Why can `std::vector<T>` hold non-copyable types like `std::unique_ptr<Foo>`?

options.text: Because `std::vector` supports move-only types via move construction and move assignment

questions.prompt: What is `if constexpr (std::is_integral_v<T>)` (C++17) used for?

options.text: Discarding the untaken branch at compile time inside templates so invalid operations in that branch don't fail compilation

questions.prompt: Select all practices that improve C++ exception safety and resource reliability. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Mark non-throwing move constructors and `swap` functions `noexcept`
Throw raw `new`-allocated pointer exceptions (`throw new MyError();`)
Wrap all owned resources (files, sockets, locks, heap memory) in RAII types
Perform mutating state commits after operations that might throw (or use copy-and-swap)

questions.prompt: What does `extern "C"` around a function declaration do in C++?

options.text: Disables C++ name mangling so the symbol can be linked against C code or loaded via `dlsym`/`GetProcAddress`

questions.prompt: What is a dangling `this` capture in an async lambda (`[this]` or `[=]` inside a member function)?

options.text: If the object is destroyed before the async callback runs, `this` becomes a dangling pointer (capture `[self = shared_from_this()]` or values instead)

questions.prompt: What does `std::views::take(5)` do when composed with an infinite range like `std::views::iota(1)`?

options.text: Lazily yields only the first 5 integers (`1..5`) without materializing an infinite container

questions.prompt: Select all valid ways to avoid unintended implicit copies in C++. (Select all that apply.)

options.text: Use `std::string_view` or `std::span` for read-only function parameters
Delete copy operations (`= delete`) on non-copyable resource handles
Pass `std::vector` by value to every read-only helper
Use `const auto&` in range-based `for` loops for non-trivial elements

questions.prompt: Why is `std::unique_lock<std::mutex>` used with `std::condition_variable` instead of `std::lock_guard`?

options.text: `condition_variable::wait` needs to unlock and re-lock the mutex repeatedly, which `unique_lock` supports and `lock_guard` does not
